subject: Architecture
title: The Millau Viaduct: Highway in the Clouds
description: One-minute skill: The Millau Viaduct: Highway in the Clouds.

hook.text: The Millau Viaduct in France is taller than the Eiffel Tower — cars drive through clouds.

buildup.text: At 1,125 feet, its tallest pier makes it the highest bridge in the world, spanning the Tarn Valley.

discovery.text: Norman Foster designed it to be as thin as possible — the deck is only 14 feet deep despite spanning 1,122 feet.

twist.text: The deck was built on both sides of the valley and pushed out over the void — sliding into position.

climax.text: Drivers report feeling like they're flying. The bridge eliminates a bottleneck that caused 4-hour delays.

punchline.text: A road through the sky. Built to save you from traffic.

quiz.question: How was the Millau Viaduct's deck constructed?
options: Lifted into place by the world's largest crane
Built from both sides and pushed out to meet in the middle
Assembled on the ground and raised hydraulically
